statusValues.partly-outdated: Mostly correct but misses a later change
statusValues.wrong-scope: Correct, but for another country, customer or team than the question

facts.topic: Birth leave Belgium (geboorteverlof / congé de naissance)
facts.truth: 20 days since 2023-01-01. First 3 days paid 100% by the employer, remaining 17 days paid by the health insurance fund (mutualiteit) at 82% of capped gross. To be taken within 4 months of the birth. Employee informs the employer.

disagree.claim: 15 days
15 days
Dutch rules: 1 week plus up to 5 weeks aanvullend geboorteverlof
Consultant told the customer 15 days

facts.truth: One working week paid 100% by the employer within 4 weeks of the birth, plus up to 5 weeks aanvullend geboorteverlof within 6 months, paid by UWV at 70% of daily wage (capped).
EUR 10 per worked day since 2026-01-01. Employer share max EUR 8.91, employee share min EUR 1.09.

disagree.claim: Consultant tells a Veldra employee EUR 8

facts.topic: Indexation cap for wages above EUR 4,000
facts.truth: Since the law of June 2026 wages above EUR 4,000 gross are only indexed on the first EUR 4,000. PC 200 indexes in January, so the first private sector effect is January 2027 (forecast 3.76%).

disagree.claim: Full salary indexed, no cap mentioned (written January 2026)
Consultant unsure, promises a callback

facts.note: No reference document exists yet. The knowledge lives in a Teams answer by Pieter and a newsletter email.

facts.topic: Belgian transposition of the EU Pay Transparency Directive
facts.truth: Belgium missed the 2026-06-07 deadline and asked for six more months. No private sector law yet. Expected late 2026 or early 2027. First reports for 250+ employees due June 2027.

disagree.claim: Belgian law in force since 7 June 2026

facts.topic: Monthly payroll input cut-off Veldra Belgium
facts.truth: The 18th of the month (service agreement annex 2025). Veldra asked in September 2026 to move it to the 17th from Q4. Not agreed yet.

disagree.claim: 20th of the month
Customer asks for the 17th (request, not agreed)

facts.topic: Escalation contact at SD Worx for Veldra Benelux
facts.truth: Sofie Hermans, service delivery manager Benelux, since March 2025.

disagree.claim: Wim Van den Broeck
Wim Van den Broeck

facts.topic: Veldra decision maker for HR and payroll
facts.truth: Charlotte Dubois, group HR director Europe, since June 2024. Paul Verbeke left Veldra in 2024.

disagree.claim: Paul Verbeke, HR director Benelux
Paul Verbeke

facts.truth: Live since 2026-07-01. Originally planned for 2026-04-01, moved because of data migration issues. Protime rollout on hold until the Betriebsrat agrees.

disagree.claim: Go-live 1 April 2026, Protime in scope for the same date
Legacy Dutch engine, migration planned for 2023

facts.truth: Veldra Iberia pays 14 salaries. Store staff get the two extra payments prorated monthly (prorrateo). Office staff get them in full in June and December. The Spanish working instruction only describes the June and December payment.

disagree.claim: All staff paid in June and December

The richest source for onboarding: Jonas explains who to call per country, what is outdated in the account plan, and the Spanish quirk. The 30 minute call from the brief, but spoken, not written.
